problem_statement: The RTIO executor does not handle an AWAIT operation when no rtio_iodev is attached to the submission. Such a 'relaxed' await should pause only that one submission chain until it is explicitly signaled via rtio_sqe_signal(), while the iodev stays free to serve unrelated submissions from other chains. Without this, a relaxed await submission either fails the chain immediately (the executor only knew CALLBACK and DELAY) or has no way to be paused-and-resumed, so it cannot be used as a logical sequencing step that does not lock a bus.

problem_statement_fixed:
The RTIO executor does not handle an AWAIT operation when no rtio_iodev is attached to the submission. Such a 'relaxed' await should pause only that one submission chain until it is explicitly signaled via rtio_sqe_signal(), while the iodev stays free to serve unrelated submissions from other chains. Without this, a relaxed await submission either fails the chain immediately (the executor only knew CALLBACK and DELAY) or has no way to be paused-and-resumed, so it cannot be used as a logical sequencing step that does not lock a bus.

To make this behavior available to callers, the public RTIO API must provide a helper `rtio_sqe_prep_await_executor(struct rtio_sqe *sqe, int8_t prio, void *userdata)` that prepares an AWAIT submission with no rtio_iodev attached. A relaxed await prepared this way must pause only the chain containing it until `rtio_sqe_signal()` is called on that SQE; while it is paused, other chains and unrelated submissions may continue, and the iodev remains free to serve them. When the SQE is signaled, the await must complete successfully and produce a CQE for that chain carrying the prepared userdata.
